variants.headline: The vote abroad went our way
body: Our effort to sway the election in a small city-state has succeeded. The result stands, and the count finished where we intended.

variants.headline: The vote abroad went against us
body: Our effort to sway the election in a small city-state has come to nothing. The count finished against us, and the coin we spent on it finished with the count.

variants.headline: The election in {{cityState}} goes our way
body: We are informed that the election in {{cityState}} has gone our government's way. A merchant who often calls at the council hall says the canvassers are already bringing back the stools they borrowed while taking names at the door.

variants.headline: Make the case for meddling
body: We tried to swing an election abroad and failed. The next minister who asks us to meddle should say what he hopes to get that an envoy couldn't win in the open. Until he makes that case, let him deal with the people the voters choose.

variants.headline: One number from a murky business
body: Strip away the rumor and one figure survives: our standing in the city-state moved by {{influence}}. Figures do not flatter themselves. Whatever else the operation achieved or cost, this is the part that can be weighed, and the next one will be weighed against it.

variants.headline: Our diplomat takes up post in {{civilization}}
body: We have posted a diplomat to {{civilization}}. The envoy will speak for us at that court, and the letters home will carry what its ministers say in rooms our traders never see.

variants.headline: Our envoy takes a post at a major court
body: We have posted an envoy to a foreign court. At the coach yard, a clerk tucked an empty dispatch pouch under the strap of the envoy's trunk; the first replies can come back in the same pouch.

variants.headline: An envoy established at {{capital}}
body: In the manner of former reigns, an envoy of ours is now established at {{capital}}, the seat of {{civilization}}. Letters will pass between the two courts, as they have since courts first learned to write.

variants.headline: A diplomat goes to {{civilization}}
body: Our diplomat is in {{civilization}} tonight. The envoy speaks for us there. The envoy also listens. In the contest of courts, an ear at another table is worth a regiment in the field.

variants.headline: A foreign spy, caught and named
body: A foreign spy at work inside our borders has been caught, and this time the watch learned whose service sent them. The government now knows exactly whom it is dealing with.

variants.headline: A foreign spy is killed in our streets
body: A foreign spy caught at work inside our borders did not survive the catching. The government knows whose service sent them, which is more than the family back home will ever be told.

variants.headline: Hear it! A spy is taken in {{cityName}}
body: Hear it, people of {{cityName}}! A foreign spy was at work in your streets, and your watch took them! Taken, and stopped! Go about your business, and sleep well: the watch is awake!

variants.headline: A foreign spy uncovered!
body: Neighbors! Our watch has uncovered a foreign spy among us. The porter who works the late door says half the street has stopped by to compare notes about its callers. Ask him again tomorrow and he'll have to charge admission.

variants.headline: Seen at the work, but not named
body: One of our spies abroad has been noticed at the work. The watchers there know an agent was operating against them, but the agent's name and employer stayed hidden.

variants.headline: What {{target}} may hold back
body: The authorities in {{target}} know a spy was at work and have not traced the agent to us. Our envoy may be spared a formal complaint. At the ministry there, clerks will be looking twice at the seals on pouches that used to travel unopened, and our diplomats will find the doors a little slower to open.

variants.headline: Our spy drew notice and may bring home {{possibleTechnology}}
body: Our agent abroad drew notice. The dispatches leave open whether the attempt yielded {{possibleTechnology}}, and an embassy clerk says he's already been asked twice why unfamiliar faces were calling at his door.

variants.headline: One of ours is marked in {{cityName}}
body: In this season our agent drew notice in {{cityName}}. A copyist there recalls how the people who once called openly began stopping at the outer door after dusk.

variants.headline: A foreign spy, seen and unnamed
body: Our watch has discovered a foreign agent at work. A clerk who heard the news took his papers with him when he went to dinner. The agent's employer is still unknown.

variants.headline: The spy who died unnamed
body: Our watchers killed a foreign spy caught at work inside our borders, and the intruder died with the name still in their teeth. Whoever sent them now waits for a letter that is not coming.

variants.headline: Notice: the watch is awake
body: This paper learns that our watchers have marked a foreign agent at work inside our borders. The employer is not yet named, but the marking itself should reassure: the government's counter-work proceeds, quietly and without panic.

variants.headline: Someone was watching {{cityName}}
body: A foreign spy has been spotted at work in {{cityName}}. Nobody knows who sent them. The market filled its stalls as usual, but people counted their change a little more carefully.

variants.headline: Named abroad, and the doors close
body: One of our spies has been identified at work abroad. The other side now knows whose agent it was, and agents who are known do not work again. The quiet work in that country is over.

variants.headline: Killed abroad, and known to them
body: One of our spies has been killed at work abroad, and the other side knows whose agent died. Whatever the operation was worth, it is ended now, and the worth is a ledger only the service will ever read.

variants.headline: Our spy is killed abroad, unnamed
body: One of our spies has been killed at work abroad. The watchers there stopped the agent without learning whose service sent them. Our hand in the matter stays hidden; the loss stays with us.

variants.headline: The ministry owes us its account
body: The authorities in {{target}} have identified a spy in our service. If the ministry keeps its explanation behind closed doors, our own citizens will have to take the other country's account on trust. Let the minister tell us what public purpose the operation served. The people who did the work can stay out of the statement.

variants.headline: The cost of the quiet work in {{target}}
body: An agent of ours is dead in {{target}}, and {{target}} knows whose. Work like this is paid for twice: once in the person, once in the trust, and both bills have arrived together. What the work bought in return, no one outside the service can yet say.

variants.headline: A winter coat passed on
body: An agent of ours has died in service abroad. At the old lodgings, the landlady gave the agent's winter coat to a traveler. She recalled a night when her lodger had come back in shirtsleeves after doing much the same.

variants.headline: Our spy may have gained {{possibleTechnology}}
body: One of our spies has finished work abroad without being noticed. The reports reaching home suggest the operation may have obtained {{possibleTechnology}} for us. If the reports hold, the forges will be the first to show it.

variants.headline: The quiet account
body: The work abroad, in short:
Detection: none. Likely gain: {{possibleTechnology}}.
The years of study we did not spend are the years we keep.

variants.headline: Unnoticed in {{target}}
body: Our people worked {{target}} tonight and were not detected. Early word says the take may include {{possibleTechnology}}. If that holds, the gap in learning between the two nations narrows. No workshop in either country will hear why.

variants.headline: Quiet win: possibly {{possibleTechnology}}
body: Nobody noticed us. Likely take: {{possibleTechnology}}. That is the whole story, and it is a good one.

variants.headline: One of ours has taken rooms in {{cityName}}
body: One of our spies is now stationed in {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}}. The work of watching that city begins from inside its walls, closer than any envoy could get.

variants.headline: A quiet posting to {{cityName}}
body: One of our people has taken a post in {{cityName}}, a city of {{civilization}}. The first letter home can say what a visiting envoy might miss: what people there talk about once their visitors have gone.

variants.headline: One of ours goes to {{cityName}}
body: It is told that one of our quieter folk has gone to live in {{cityName}}, in the land of {{civilization}}. They will walk the markets, mind the talk, and send home what the wind carries.

variants.headline: A room inside {{cityName}}
body: We now have an agent in {{cityName}}. A count of the wagons passing the same window every morning can tell us something the occasional dispatch from {{civilization}} cannot: whether a long train at the gate is ordinary traffic or something new.

variants.headline: A diplomat of {{civilization}} arrives at our capital
body: The new envoy has taken up residence at our capital. At the foreign ministry, the gatekeeper has a new face to learn and a new name for the visitors' book. A question meant for {{civilization}} now has a door to knock on instead of a courier to wait for.

variants.headline: A foreign diplomat arrives
body: A foreign diplomat has taken up a post in the capital. At the council hall, a merchant carrying a customs bill asked a clerk how to arrange a meeting. “My cloth has sat on their quay for a month,” she said. “They send me a bill every week, so I know it's still there.”

variants.headline: An envoy from {{civilization}} at our court
body: This paper is pleased to record that an envoy of {{civilization}} is now received at our capital. Governments that speak directly have less cause to speak sharply, and words that travel by envoy arrive with fewer dents than words that travel by rumor.

variants.headline: A listener at our table
body: A diplomat of {{civilization}} has taken rooms at our capital, and a good guest listens more than speaks. Hospitality is cheap; a map left on the dining room wall is not. Let the steward pour the wine and the clerks keep the papers in the study. A bored envoy writes a thin report home.
